findings.title: GPU pricing started on 2026-09-22; main-account allowances were not resized
paras: Until 2026-09-22 a GPU job cost about one credit per CPU (a 32-GPU b200 job on 2026-08-18: 100 credits a minute; the same job now: 104,288). Since then each GPU type has its own price (a typical GPU job costs about 250× more), but the standard main-account allowance stayed at 10,800,000 credits a month — now only about 96 H100-hours or 324 A100-hours. That is why so many main accounts ran out within days. (Project and condo accounts have no such allowance; they are limited only by GPUs at once.)
Ask: are the main-account allowances meant to be this small, or due to be resized?

findings.title: Main accounts are told 0 GPU-hours; their credit allowance runs out long before
paras: This is about each lab's main account — the one named after the PI (e.g. `ayuille1`) that everyone in the lab submits to by default. For it, `sbalance` shows 0 GPU-hours and 0 CPU core-hours, but a third limit on the same account — 10,800,000 credits a month — always runs out first (table). It resets on the 1st; in between, used credits halve every 30 days (about 7.4 A100-hours of room back per day). `sbalance` also sums the whole quarter, so its numbers do not match what Slurm enforces.
Project and condo accounts are not affected: their credit budget is so large it never runs out, and what limits them is the number of GPUs they may hold at once.

findings.title: 36 labs have used 80% or more of this month's main allowance (11 have no other account)
paras: New jobs on the main account wait (`AssocGrpBillingMinutes`) until 2026-11-01 or until fading frees room. Labs with project/condo accounts keep running there (no hour limit); labs with only a main account are stopped.

findings.title: Going over the main-account allowance ends all of that account's running jobs (202 times in 14 days)
paras: When a main account passes its allowance, Slurm ends all of its running jobs at once (recorded as `TIMEOUT` before their time limit). Since 2026-10-03: 202 times, 37 accounts, 1,062 jobs holding 1,062 GPUs (391 of them CPU-only). Jobs on the lab's project or condo accounts are not affected. It is not charged as money — compute is free for now.

Cause: AccountingStorageEnforce=associations,limits,qos has no `safe` (Slurm's docs: jobs "launched but then killed when the limit is reached"). Ask: enable `safe` so jobs wait instead of dying, and email labs at 80-90%.

tables.caption: Accounts whose running jobs were ended at the limit

findings.title: Root cause: no per-person limits on compute or storage
paras: Every limit on Skipjack is per lab: one monthly allowance per main account, one GPUs-at-once cap per project account, one quota per lab directory. Inside a lab it is first come, first served. Of 1,273 person-account pairs, none has a per-person monthly limit; on project accounts the per-person cap equals the account's (16/32/64 GPUs), so one person may hold all of it; no lab has an account coordinator (0 on the cluster), so PIs cannot set limits for their own members.

What it costs the others (last 30 days): in 20 of 37 labs where 3+ people used GPUs, one person used more than half of the lab's GPU-hours; 51,378 GPU-hours were used beyond twice an equal share. 44 people in 16 labs waited 1,687 hours in all for their own project account while a single lab-mate held half or more of its GPUs. Since 2026-10-03, a lab going over its main allowance ended running jobs 202 times (1,062 jobs of 80 people; 25 times several people's jobs at once).

Suggestion — each piece is a standard feature Skipjack already uses somewhere (26 people have their own GPU cap on condo accounts; home folders have per-person quotas): (1) GPUs at once per person, e.g. half a project account (`MaxTRESPerUser=gres/gpu=8` on QOS `jhu`), and 2 GPUs / 8 hours for interactive sessions; (2) GPU-hours per person (`GrpTRESMins` on each person's association, e.g. about twice an equal share of a main allowance) — it fades over 30 days and resets on the 1st, so it is a monthly budget; a strictly weekly one needs a weekly reset script; (3) `safe` in AccountingStorageEnforce, so a job that would overrun a budget waits instead of being killed; (4) each PI coordinator of their own accounts, so labs can raise or lower these themselves; (5) a WEKA directory quota on each person's folder inside the lab directory (WEKA 4.4 has no per-user quotas).

findings.title: Project accounts have no hour limit, only a GPUs-at-once cap
paras: 60 PIs have project accounts (PI_project, e.g. `jgray21_disc`). Their --credit budget would last ? months even with 16 H100s busy non-stop, so the only real limit is 16 GPUs at once (32 or 64 for a few): at most 16 × 744 h = 11,904 GPU-hours this month. Four project accounts = 64 GPUs at once, while the 102 PIs with only a main account get its allowance: about 96 H100-hours a month.

findings.title: Monthly capacity differs by up to 368× between labs once project accounts are counted
paras: A plain lab has only the standard main allowance: 10,800,000 credits a month ($180 at ARCH's implied prices, about 324 A100-hours). Each project account adds up to 16 GPUs at once (32 or 64 for a few) — at most 11,904 GPU-hours in a 31-day month. 59 of 137 JHU labs differ from a plain lab; the ceilings below assume every project GPU runs all month, although the caps add up to 5.3× the GPUs that exist.

findings.title: Project accounts, not main-account allowances, decide who gets the GPUs
paras: Since 2026-09-22, the 59 JHU labs with project or condo accounts used 95% of all JHU GPU-hours; the 78 labs with only a main account used 5%. The GPUs-at-once caps add up to 1,796 GPUs against 340 in the JHU partitions, so a cap is not a guarantee: an active project account uses about 1,376 GPU-hours a month (median; busiest 10,018). `sbalance` shows each project as "100,000,000 GPU-hours allocated" — the source of claims of hundreds of millions of hours.

Project accounts also carry 556× a main account's fairshare weight, so the same labs are first in line. Ask: tie caps and shares to the size of the approved allocation rather than to the number of accounts.

findings.title: Project accounts are set up to be billed to the PI; prices are not published
paras: Main accounts run on the free QOS `scavenger` (free list: `all`, `scavenger`, `ssci`); the project QOS `jhu`/`jhu2`/`jhu4` are billable to the cost center a PI must attach before a project is created. Billing is enforced, but every rate is $0.00 today (ARCH: no billing without notice).

ARCH's cost preview reads the billing weights as 0.1 cent per hour, which implies the prices below: a typical active project would cost about $1,304 a month (top quarter $4,570 or more; busiest $21,176), and the standard main allowance is worth $180 (the submit tool calls it a "weekly cap" although it resets monthly). Ask: publish the rates, any cap per project or per PI, and whether main accounts stay free.

findings.title: Queue priority works against main accounts inside a department
paras: Priority = fairshare (up to 20,000 points) + time waiting (up to 5,000, reached after 7 days) + job size (up to 5,000). Slurm ranks schools first, then departments, then the accounts inside a department by their shares: a main account has 180,000, a project or condo account 100,000,000 (556×). So main accounts rank behind project accounts that have used far more — right now 60 main accounts in 12 departments.

In csci (433 people) the median fairshare score is 0.102 on main accounts and 0.251 on project/condo accounts (2.5×) — about 2,969 priority points, or 4.2 days of waiting in the queue. School order right now: ap (0% of recent use) > IT / ARCH-managed (0% of recent use) > Public Health (0% of recent use) > gp (0% of recent use) > jh (0% of recent use) > Medicine (0% of recent use) > Arts & Sciences (7% of recent use) > Engineering (92% of recent use).

findings.title: Storage limits are inconsistent
paras: Scratch limits (/weka/scratch/jhu/PI or /weka/scratch/schmidt/PI) range from 1 TB to 70 TB with no obvious rule, and 14 directories have no limit at all (`arochab1`, `bblanch6`, `bgermro1`, `dzarzhitsky`, `ext-mwang131`, `jperafa1`, `kniebuh1`, `mprotzm2`, `rdesouz4`, `sponoma1`, `ssci-aviralku`, `ssci-jbt`, `ssci-rus`, `ssci-ys-shigroup`). Only 18 of 162 labs have a project filesystem (/weka/projects/PI, 500G to 500T). Not matching any lab's account: `admin`, `a user`, `mallada`, `sj-estimator`, `vandurme`.

findings.title: 46 of 604 GPUs (8%) cannot run jobs right now
paras: Some nodes are held by admin reservations (testing, burn-in) or are down/draining. B200 and B300 nodes are only open to Schmidt accounts; the other GPU partitions only to JHU accounts.

glossary: Main account

The Slurm account named after the PI (e.g. `ayuille1`). Everyone in the lab submits to it by default. It has a monthly allowance of billing credits and no limit on GPUs at once, and its jobs are free (QOS `scavenger`).
Project account

An extra account a PI can request for a specific project, named PI_project (e.g. `jgray21_disc`). No practical monthly limit, but capped at 16 GPUs at once (32 or 64 for a few). Its jobs are billable to the project's cost center (rates are $0 today).
Cost center
A JHU budget number a PI attaches to a project in ARCH's portal; billable project usage would be charged to it.
Implied price
ARCH's billing code treats each billing unit as 0.1 cent per hour, so the cluster's weights already imply a price list (e.g. A100 $0.555, H100 $1.876 per GPU-hour). Not charged today.
Condo account
An account for GPUs a PI bought into (`*_h200`, `*_rtx6000`). It guarantees access to that many GPUs of that type.
Billing credits
What Slurm charges a running job every minute (Slurm calls them billing-minutes). The price depends on the hardware: e.g. one H100 costs 1,876 credits per minute, one A100 555.
Monthly allowance

The number of credits a main account may spend per calendar month, shared by everyone in the lab. It resets on the 1st. When it runs out, new jobs on the main account wait (reason `AssocGrpBillingMinutes`). Only main accounts have one that matters: project and condo accounts have a credit budget so large it never runs out.
Usage fading
Between resets, older usage slowly counts less: it halves every 30 days. A main account that has spent its allowance gets a small amount back each day.
GPUs at once
A cap on how many GPUs an account (or one user) may hold at the same moment, regardless of how long they run. Project and condo accounts have one (16, 32 or 64); main accounts do not.
Queue priority
When GPUs are busy, waiting jobs start in priority order. Up to 20,000 points come from fairshare, up to 5,000 from time spent waiting (full after 7 days), up to 5,000 from job size.
Fairshare
The part of queue priority that rewards groups that have used little recently compared with their entitlement. Scored 0 to 1; higher starts sooner.
Shares

A group's entitlement in the fairshare calculation, set by the admins. Only the ratio between groups competing at the same level matters: a main account has 180,000, each project or condo account 100,000,000.
QOS
Quality of service: a named bundle of limits attached to an account (e.g. `jhu` = 16 GPUs at once).
Partition
A group of nodes with the same GPU type, e.g. `h100`, `a100`.
Reservation
Nodes set aside by the admins (maintenance, testing, burn-in); ordinary jobs cannot use them.
GPU tiers
High = B300, B200, H200, H100. Mid = A100, RTX PRO 6000. Low = L40S and A100 MIG slices. Based on the cluster's own price per GPU.
MIG slice
A fraction of an A100 (2g.20gb = 20 GB) offered on the `interactive_gpu` partition.
